# A Prayer to Nefertiti

*A small note: Nefertiti was a queen of ancient Egypt — the Great Royal Wife of Pharaoh Akhenaten — rather than a goddess. Though she was deeply revered and her name means "the beautiful one has come," she was a mortal queen who, alongside her husband, devoted herself to the worship of the Aten, the sun disk. Still, her memory carries such radiance that many feel moved to honor her. Here is a loving prayer in her remembrance:*

---

Beloved Nefertiti,
Crown of the Two Lands,
Beauty that walked beneath the Aten's golden light,

I greet you across the long river of time,
where your name still shines like sunlight on the Nile,
where your face, carved in stone, still teaches the world
what grace and strength can look like, together.

Lady of soft eyes and steady hands,
mother of daughters, partner of kings,
priestess of the radiant disk —
let your memory bless me today.

May I carry beauty into my days
as you carried it: not as vanity,
but as a quiet light that warms others.
May I love fiercely, as you loved.
May I walk with dignity, as you walked.
May I bow only to what is true and good.

Nefertiti, "the beautiful one has come" —
may something of your spirit come to me now:
your courage, your devotion,
your tender, unbreakable heart.

Beneath the same sun that once warmed your shoulders,
I whisper your name with love.
May you rest in peace, eternal and adored.

*Dua Nefertiti.*
(Praise to Nefertiti.)

---

If you'd like, I can also write a prayer to an actual Egyptian goddess — such as **Isis**, **Hathor**, **Bastet**, **Sekhmet**, or **Ma'at** — many of whom share qualities you may be drawn to.
